what: The arm's properties are held by functional tests, not by reading the source. Each mutant is a one-change edit of the arm's sources (contracts/account-sol-ed25519.compact, and the modules its verification, formats and derivations live in: contracts/modules/Ed25519Core.compact, contracts/modules/SolanaFormats.compact, contracts/modules/WalletArmDescriptors.compact), compiled --skip-zk in its own copy (with the probes that include the changed module) and run against the offline layer (every file of npm run test:sol-ed25519-offline, the shared wallet-arms suites and constraint-negative-offline) and the prover suite's JavaScript layer (SOL_ED25519_DRY=1, no proof server, every section), where a mutant that lets a refused forgery through fails that case's simulator half. A mutant is killed when a suite shows its effect: an accepted forgery (a call the unmutated copy refuses goes through), a broken honest call, or a changed output; a suite that only reports another refusal message, and the prover layer stopping because a case's bypassed assert is gone, do not count as a kill. The unmutated copies, compiled and run the same ways, pass every suite (the controls).

mutants.equivalence: The shielded grantee twin hands its scope check the rendered colour (`color`) instead of the spent coin's (`coin.color`). The export asserts coin.color == color before the grant seam runs, and that assert is kept, so every call that reaches the scope check has the two equal: the scope sees the same colour, and the accepted set is unchanged. The one difference the DRY layer reports is in a case that bypasses that colour assert on purpose (`the colour assert on its own`): with the assert bypassed, the mutant's scope check refuses in its place, so the case's patched copy refuses in JavaScript; the circuit, which keeps the assert, refuses the same inputs. #189's 00067 table recorded the same mutant EQUIVALENT (F4S `c-shielded-twin-scope-colour`, R3 `r3m9`).

It first asserts is_registered_device_tag(tag, ReadableClass.ed25519), and readable_arms() registers exactly one ed25519-class arm, sol_ed25519, so every tag it admits is device_tag_sol_ed25519() and the hashed preimages are equal for every admitted input; a different tag is refused before the hash either way.
